exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong fundraiser plan tracks the goal with equations and inequalities — here is how one student ran a book drive.

traits.trait: Models the goal as an equation
traits.sample: We need 240 books and have 85, so 85 + b = 240 tells me we still need b = 155 books.
traits.why: The unknown is defined and the equation mirrors the situation.

traits.sample: To hit our goal we need b ≥ 155 — any amount at or above 155 works, which is why it is an inequality, not an equation.
traits.why: It explains WHY the ≥ symbol fits the real goal.

traits.sample: We collect about 22 books per day, so 155 ÷ 22 ≈ 7 more days — I rounded up because a partial day still counts.
traits.why: The projection shows the division and defends the rounding.

traits.sample: We are at 85 of 240, which is 35% — behind the halfway mark, so I proposed a weekend collection table.
traits.why: The math leads directly to an action plan.
